_meta.what: Ahmedabad's 'pothole economy' — the recurring build/dig/rebuild road cycle and the contractors who repeatedly win AMC road & bridge work. Companion to rent_capture/ahmedabad.json (land) and docs/the-double-extraction.md, which names road contracts as 'the purest case' of road-building-as-a-rent. Each entry: {item, contractor, value, year, tier, claim, source, denial_if_any, verify}.

tier_legend.A: DOCUMENTED FACT — AMC's own blacklist/contractor circulars, standing-committee / budget figures, official audit (Local Fund / municipal auditor) findings, lab test reports, FIRs, named project records. Stated as fact, with source.
tier_legend.B: REPORTED ALLEGATION — corporator-contractor-engineer nexus, kickback, cartel/L1-rigging, deliberately poor work. Framed as 'alleged/reported by [named source]', NEVER asserted; denials included where on record.
tier_legend.C: ANALYSIS — the mechanism / our reading (e.g. why bad work guarantees the next tender). Not a factual claim about any named party's conduct.

_meta.hard_rule: PUBLIC repo naming private firms. A contractor is NAMED ONLY where an AMC document, audit, lab report or FIR documents it (tier A). The 'nexus / cartel / kickback' framing is tier B or C and is NEVER asserted as fact against any named firm. No fabrication; verify:true where a figure or detail is uncertain.
_meta.frame: Harvey/Ambedkar 'double extraction' (docs/the-double-extraction.md): the contractor is the pivot who pockets the gap between contract value and suppressed wage; 'road contracts are the purest case — recurring (build, dig up, rebuild), opaque, and quality-indifferent, because bad work GUARANTEES the next tender.' The pothole economy is not a failure of road-building; it is road-building AS A RENT.
_meta.status: Authored 2026-06 from AMC's own published blacklist circular, official budget/standing-committee figures, the Local Fund / municipal audit record, multi-lab test reports and named reporting (Gujarat Samachar, DeshGujarat, DNA). Allegation entries cite the named source and any stated position.

entries.item: AMC annual road spend / the resurfacing cycle (the macro figure)
entries.contractor: (multiple; AMC Road Project & Road & Building Dept)
entries.value: ~Rs 1,000 crore/year on road build + resurfacing + pothole repair; FY2025-26 budget ~Rs 1,200 crore for ~550 km of new TP road + resurfacing (in a Rs 14,001 cr total budget)
entries.claim: AMC spends on the order of Rs 1,000 crore a year building, resurfacing and patching roads; the FY2025-26 budget earmarked roughly Rs 1,200 crore for ~550 km of new TP road and resurfacing. The road network is ~2,500-2,580 km of bituminous road served by only ~940 km of stormwater drainage — so monsoon water has nowhere to go and the same stretches fail, are patched, and are re-tarred year after year.
entries.source: Gujarat Samachar (English), 'From metro city to pothole city: Ahmedabad riddled with damaged roads' and 'City of potholes: Ahmedabad spends Rs 1.20 crore on damaged roads' (~Rs 1,000 cr/yr; 2,500+ km roads vs 940 km drainage); 'AMC budget of Rs 14,001 cr presented to Standing Committee' / Elets eGov (FY2025-26, ~550 km, ~Rs 1,200 cr).

entries.item: Zonal carve-up of resurfacing work (from AMC's own DLP-Road registers)
entries.contractor: Apex Protech LLP; Keystone Infrastructure Pvt Ltd; Maruti Construction; M/s L.G. Chaudhary; Vimal Construction; Nar Narayan Infrastructure Pvt Ltd; Ashish Infracon Pvt Ltd; Fortune Builders; R.K.C. Infrabuild Pvt Ltd; N.C.C. Infra Pvt Ltd; Milan Road Buildtech LLP; K.E.C.L. (transliterations HITL-pending, verify against MCA)
entries.value: 1,683 road segments across SEVEN published registers (2017-18, 2018-19, 2019-20, 2020-21, 2022-23, 2024-25, 2025-26; no 2021-22 or 2023-24 published)
entries.claim: AMC's own published Defect-Liability-Period (DLP) Road registers — the documents that name the contractor liable for each resurfaced stretch — show the city's entire resurfacing programme carried by a CLOSED SET of ~7 firms whose zonal dominance ROTATES in multi-year blocks. Examples over the 7-year panel: North zone held by N.C.C. Infra 2017-18→2019-20 (10, 32, 13 segments) then taken by Apex Protech LLP 2024-25→2025-26 (17, 29); West held by L.G. Chaudhary (50 segments in 2018-19) then ceded to Apex Protech (34, 20); Central locked by Maruti Construction 2022-23→2025-26 (18, 14, 16); South/South-West dominated for years by Nar Narayan Infrastructure (53 segments in South-West alone in 2022-23); North-West by Maruti Infracreation 2019-21 then Keystone (73) in 2025-26. The 2017-18 register names individual proprietors/partners; by 2024-26 the same work is held by AA-class Pvt-Ltd firms — the market consolidated. Money concentrates in west-side developed wards (Naroda, Paldi, Gota, Sarkhej, Navrangpura). This is a documented distribution pattern from AMC's own records; it is NOT a claim that any award was rigged (that remains the tier-B nexus entry below).
entries.source: Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation DLP Road registers, served by the AMC document API ViewFile?TYPE=FileRepository,<id> — IDs 315 (2017-18), 316 (2018-19), 317 (2019-20), 318 (2020-21), 319 (2022-23), 2424 (2024-25), 2628 (2025-26). Parsed in sevent4 scripts/recipes/ahmedabad/parse_resurfaced_registers.py → data/cities/ahmedabad/source/budget/roads/ (roads_resurfaced_rows.csv, panel_7yr_summary.json, resurfacing_by_ward.geojson, contractor_registry.json). Method + linkage results: docs/ahmedabad-road-contractors-method.md §6.
entries.denial_if_any: Zonal concentration in a public works programme can reflect geographic lotting of tenders, not collusion; firm-level political linkage is unproven here and is held as tier-B pending electoral-bond/MCA/affidavit evidence. Firm-name transliterations from legacy-font Gujarati are HITL-pending and must be confirmed against MCA before any firm is named as fact in public.

entries.value: ~Rs 50 crore over four years on 363 potholes; Rs 1.20 crore in Sept 2024 on 44 potholes; a separate Rs 10 crore resurfacing allocation
entries.claim: AMC spent roughly Rs 50 crore over four years repairing 363 potholes, and Rs 1.20 crore in a single month (Sept 2024) on 44 potholes — yet with the first rain the same potholes resurface. After one spell 220 roads were dug up and 105 areas flooded. The corporation has no policy to prevent potholes from drainage/manhole failures, with repairs lagging 10-15 days. This is the recurrence the 'pothole economy' names.
entries.source: Gujarat Samachar (English): 'From metro city to pothole city' (Rs 50 cr / 363 potholes; Rs 1,000 cr/yr); 'City of potholes: Rs 1.20 crore... 44 potholes'; '220 roads dug up, 105 areas flooded, AMC still planning after monsoon hits'; 'Potholes persist in Godrej Garden City and Nikol despite AMC's Rs 10 crore allocation'.

entries.item: Hatkeshwar flyover — built, failed in ~4 years, demolished & rebuilt (the flagship quality-failure case)
entries.contractor: Ajay Engineering Infrastructure Pvt Ltd (AEIPL) — contractor; SGS India Pvt Ltd — project management consultant
entries.value: Built ~Rs 34 crore (2015-2017); demolition re-tendered at ~Rs 9.31 crore; AMC resolved to recover demolition + reconstruction cost from the contractor
entries.year: built 2015-2017, opened 2017; closed 2022; demolition ordered 15 Apr 2023
entries.claim: The Hatkeshwar flyover, built by Ajay Engineering Infrastructure Pvt Ltd (consultant SGS India Pvt Ltd) at ~Rs 34 crore and opened in 2017, deteriorated so badly it was shut to traffic by 2022 — against a design life of decades. Four independent labs (IIT Roorkee, Ecube Concrete Consultant, KCT Lab, CMAC) found the concrete/structure substandard. On 15 Apr 2023 Commissioner M. Thennarasan ordered demolition and reconstruction; AMC blacklisted BOTH the contractor and the consultant, filed a police complaint naming individuals from the two firms (Ramesh Patel, Rasik Patel, Chirag Patel, Kalpesh Patel, Amit Thakkar, Shashi Jogani, Nilam Patel), and resolved to levy the demolition/rebuild cost on the contractor. This is the strongest documented quality-failure-before-design-life finding in AMC road/bridge work.
entries.source: DeshGujarat, 'AMC to demolish and rebuild a four-year old defunct Hatkeshwar flyover bridge due to poor quality' (16 Apr 2023) and 'Hatkeshwar flyover demolition gains momentum as 4 firms submit bids' (28 Jun 2025); Gujarat Samachar (English), 'Hatkeshwar flyover: Taxpayer funds washed away in failed structure'; VibesOfIndia, 'Ahmedabad's Flyovers Expose Planning Failures and Political Stakes'.
entries.denial_if_any: The contractor and consultant contested the action and the blacklisting through legal channels (industry-standard challenge to blacklisting orders; specific firm-level denials should be cited per filing). AMC's recovery of the full demolition+reconstruction cost from the contractor was, as of reporting, still being pursued, not completed.

entries.item: Hatkeshwar contractor's continued AMC work (the 'bad work guarantees the next tender' datum)
entries.contractor: Ajay Infrastructure (Ajay Engineering Infrastructure / associated Ajay entity)
entries.value: Reported additional payment of ~Rs 26 crore on the Pallav flyover; penalty of ~Rs 2.37 crore proposed for delays but only ~Rs 23.69 lakh actually recovered
entries.claim: Per reporting, despite the Hatkeshwar failure the Ajay Infrastructure entity continued to draw AMC bridge work — an additional ~Rs 26 crore on the Pallav flyover — while of a ~Rs 2.37 crore delay penalty proposed against it, only ~Rs 23.69 lakh was actually recovered. The audit also found bills paid before completion, missing bill dates, and inadequate material oversight. This is the documented core of the mechanism: the firm whose structure failed kept getting paid and kept getting work.
entries.source: Gujarat Samachar (English), 'Hatkeshwar flyover: Taxpayer funds washed away in failed structure' (Rs 26 cr Pallav payment; Rs 2.37 cr penalty proposed, Rs 23.69 lakh recovered; bills paid pre-completion; missing dates; weak material oversight).
entries.denial_if_any: The firm has contested AMC's adverse actions; the Pallav payment is a separate awarded contract, not an admission of wrongdoing on Hatkeshwar. Penalty/recovery figures are as reported and should be re-confirmed against AMC standing-committee records.

entries.item: AMC 'Road Project' (RP) department blacklist — road-quality blacklisting on the official register
entries.contractor: Akash Infra Project Pvt Ltd; GPC Infra Pvt Ltd (both dept 'RP' = Road Project)
entries.value: n/a (punitive action, not a contract value)
entries.year: circular 10/11-Oct-2017, resolution no. 597 dated 29-Aug-2017, period to 28-Aug-2020
entries.claim: On AMC's own published 'List of Black List / Punished Contractors' (updated to 04-Jan-2023), the only entries flagged explicitly for ROAD QUALITY are two Road Project (RP) department firms — Akash Infra Project Pvt Ltd and GPC Infra Pvt Ltd — punished under resolution 597 (29-Aug-2017): the note states that within the Defect Liability Period they must fulfil tender terms and 'complete the demaged [damaged] Road work, otherwise may declare permanent Black List.' i.e. AMC's own record documents road work that failed within the defect-liability window.
entries.source: Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation, official PDF 'LIST OF BLACK LIST / PUNISHED CONTRACTORS, UPDATED UP TO 04/01/2023' (ahmedabadcity.gov.in/Uploads/FormsFonts/Contractors/LIST_OF_BLACK_LISTCONTRACTORES_UP_TO_04012023.pdf), entries 67/68 (general) = 31/32 (current), dept 'RP'.

entries.item: AMC blacklist register — overall scale (context for how rarely road firms are permanently barred)
entries.contractor: (72 general-list + 40 current-list entries across all departments)
entries.claim: AMC's published blacklist register carries on the order of 70+ historical and ~40 current punished-contractor entries across ALL departments (zones, water, bridge, housing, stores, garden) over 2006-2021 — but only a handful sit in the Road Project department and only two (Akash Infra, GPC Infra) are tagged to road-quality/defect-liability failure. Bridge-project firms (e.g. Manibhai & Brothers, the Ravi Builders JV) and a housing firm (MV Omani) appear, but the register shows road resurfacing failures rarely translate into a permanent road-firm bar.
entries.source: Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation official blacklist PDF (as above), full table 2006-2021.

entries.item: Local Fund / municipal audit of AMC bridge work — inflated bills & tender-norm breaches
entries.contractor: (contractor unnamed in the report cited; Omkar/Memco railway overbridge, North Zone)
entries.value: Rs 19.34 lakh barricade payment flagged; overhead paid at 5% and profit at 10% against a 3% tender cap
entries.claim: An AMC audit report flagged the Omkar railway overbridge (Memco, North Zone): the contractor was paid 5% overhead and 10% contract profit on extra items though tender rules cap overhead at 3%; AMC paid Rs 19.34 lakh for a barricade it may itself have owned; materials were paid at market rates instead of AMC's approved Statement of Rates; and steel/cement purchase bills were missing. This documents the bill-inflation and weak-controls pattern that underwrites the rent.
entries.source: DNA India (Ahmedabad), 'AMC's audit report raises brows: Bills for railway overbridge inflated' (dnaindia.com/ahmedabad/report-amc-s-audit-report-raises-brows-bills-for-railway-overbridge-inflated-1714079).
entries.denial_if_any: AMC/the executing department typically responds to Local-Fund audit paras with explanations; the audit para is a finding, not an adjudicated charge. Re-confirm contractor identity before naming.

entries.item: The corporator-contractor-engineer nexus / repeat-L1 cartel (the framing — NOT asserted)
entries.claim: REPORTED/ALLEGED as a pattern, not asserted against any named firm: critics and opposition corporators repeatedly allege that AMC road and infrastructure tenders flow to a stable set of well-connected firms, that deliberately substandard work is tolerated because it guarantees recurring re-tarring contracts, and that engineers signing off on bills, the standing committee approving them, and corporators are part of one chain. Gujarat Samachar's own 'Rs 1,000 crore spent annually... by municipal authority, CONTRACTORS AND POLITICIANS' framing gestures at this. NO AMC/audit document cited here names a cartel or proves rigging; this remains an attributed allegation/analysis, not a finding.
entries.source: Gujarat Samachar (English) pothole-economy coverage (the 'authority, contractors and politicians' framing); AMC leader-of-opposition allegations of 'flawed execution by contractors' (e.g. DeshGujarat, 'AMC leader of opposition alleges flawed execution in KhariCut redevelopment project', 24 Jun 2024). General Indian road-sector commentary on repeat-L1 / quality-indifference.
entries.denial_if_any: AMC and the firms concerned reject any suggestion of a cartel or deliberate poor work; tenders are issued through nprocure/AMC e-tendering on an L1 basis and awards are placed before the standing committee. No cartel finding has been adjudicated.

entries.item: The mechanism — why bad road work pays (analysis)
entries.claim: ANALYSIS: road resurfacing is the ideal rent vehicle because it is (1) RECURRING — every monsoon dissolves the surface, so demand is permanent and self-renewing; (2) OPAQUE — buried layers, thickness and bitumen content can't be verified after laying, so under-specification is near-costless to detect; (3) QUALITY-INDIFFERENT in its incentives — a road that fails within its design life does not end the relationship, it generates the NEXT patch, the NEXT resurfacing tender and the NEXT pothole-repair bill. With ~2,500 km of road on ~940 km of drainage and no anti-pothole policy, structural failure is guaranteed and continuously monetised. The defect-liability period exists precisely to break this — and AMC's own blacklist note ('complete the demaged Road work') shows it is invoked, but the Hatkeshwar pattern (Rs 26 cr more to the failed-flyover firm; Rs 23.69 lakh of a Rs 2.37 cr penalty recovered) shows how weakly the cost is clawed back.
entries.source: Analysis built on the tier-A entries above + docs/the-double-extraction.md ('road contracts are the purest case... bad work guarantees the next tender... the pothole economy... road-building AS A RENT').
